passages.text: Wisdom has built her house; she has carved out her seven pillars.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is the subject.
Wisdom acts with skill and understanding.
Wisdom has built her house.
She made her house strong and lasting.
She carved out seven pillars for her house.
These pillars support and complete her house.
passages.original: חָ֭כְמוֹת בָּנְתָ֣ה בֵיתָ֑הּ חָצְבָ֖ה עַמּוּדֶ֣יהָ שִׁבְעָֽה׃

passages.text: She has prepared her meat and mixed her wine; she has also set her table.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is a woman.
She has prepared her meat.
She has mixed her wine.
She has set her table.
passages.original: טָבְחָ֣ה טִ֭בְחָהּ מָסְכָ֣ה יֵינָ֑הּ אַ֝֗ף עָֽרְכָ֥ה שֻׁלְחָנָֽהּ׃

passages.text: She has sent out her maidservants; she calls out from the heights of the city.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is a woman.
She acts with purpose.
She sends out her maidservants.
She gives them a task.
She calls out to people.
She calls from the high places of the city.
She wants everyone to hear her.
passages.original: שָֽׁלְחָ֣ה נַעֲרֹתֶ֣יהָ תִקְרָ֑א עַל־ גַּ֝פֵּ֗י מְרֹ֣מֵי קָֽרֶת׃

passages.text: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is a woman.
She calls out to people.
She sees someone who is simple.
A simple person does not have wisdom.
She says to the simple person, “Turn in here.”
She also sees someone who lacks judgment.
A person who lacks judgment does not understand what is right.
She speaks to him.
She invites him to come to her.
passages.original: מִי־ פֶ֭תִי יָסֻ֣ר הֵ֑נָּה חֲסַר־ לֵ֝֗ב אָ֣מְרָה לּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom speaks to those who lack understanding.
She invites them to her feast.
She says, “Come.”
“Eat my bread.”
“Drink the wine I have prepared.”
passages.original: לְ֭כוּ לַחֲמ֣וּ בְֽלַחֲמִ֑י וּ֝שְׁת֗וּ בְּיַ֣יִן מָסָֽכְתִּי׃

passages.text: Leave your folly behind, and you will live; walk in the way of understanding.”
passages.sermon:
Foolish people act without wisdom.
Leave behind your foolish ways.
If you do this, you will live.
Choose to walk in the way of understanding.
Follow the path of wisdom.
passages.original: עִזְב֣וּ פְתָאיִ֣ם וִֽחְי֑וּ וְ֝אִשְׁר֗וּ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ בִּינָֽה׃

passages.text: He who corrects a mocker brings shame on himself; he who rebukes a wicked man taints himself.
passages.sermon:
A mocker is a person who scorns wisdom and instruction.
A wicked man rejects correction and does evil.
If you correct a mocker, you bring shame on yourself.
If you rebuke a wicked man, you harm your own reputation.
passages.original: יֹ֤סֵ֨ר׀ לֵ֗ץ לֹקֵ֣חַֽ ל֣וֹ קָל֑וֹן וּמוֹכִ֖יחַ לְרָשָׁ֣ע מוּמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not rebuke a mocker, or he will hate you; rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.
passages.sermon:
A mocker rejects correction.
Do not rebuke a mocker.
If you rebuke a mocker, he will hate you.
A wise man values correction.
Rebuke a wise man.
If you rebuke a wise man, he will love you.
passages.original: אַל־ תּ֣וֹכַח לֵ֭ץ פֶּן־ יִשְׂנָאֶ֑ךָּ הוֹכַ֥ח לְ֝חָכָ֗ם וְיֶאֱהָבֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Instruct a wise man, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous man, and he will increase his learning.
passages.sermon:
A wise man listens to instruction.
He becomes even wiser.
A righteous man receives teaching.
He gains more understanding.
passages.original: תֵּ֣ן לְ֭חָכָם וְיֶחְכַּם־ ע֑וֹד הוֹדַ֥ע לְ֝צַדִּ֗יק וְי֣וֹסֶף לֶֽקַח׃פ

passages.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom begins with fearing the LORD.
The LORD is God.
To fear the LORD means to respect and honor Him.
This is the first step to true wisdom.
Knowing the Holy One brings understanding.
The Holy One is God.
Understanding comes from knowing God.
passages.original: תְּחִלַּ֣ת חָ֭כְמָה יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים בִּינָֽה׃

passages.text: For through wisdom your days will be multiplied, and years will be added to your life.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom gives you many days.
Wisdom adds years to your life.
Wisdom increases your lifespan.
Wisdom brings long life.
passages.original: כִּי־ בִ֭י יִרְבּ֣וּ יָמֶ֑יךָ וְיוֹסִ֥יפוּ לְּ֝ךָ֗ שְׁנ֣וֹת חַיִּֽים׃

passages.text: If you are wise, you are wise to your own advantage; but if you scoff, you alone will bear the consequences.
passages.sermon:
A wise person benefits himself.
If you act with wisdom, you gain for yourself.
If you mock or scoff, you suffer alone.
You alone bear the results of your actions.

passages.text: The woman named Folly is loud; she is naive and knows nothing.
passages.sermon:
Folly is a woman.
She is loud.
She is naive.
She does not know anything.
passages.original: אֵ֣שֶׁת כְּ֭סִילוּת הֹֽמִיָּ֑ה פְּ֝תַיּ֗וּת וּבַל־ יָ֥דְעָה מָּֽה׃

passages.text: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the heights of the city, calling out to those who pass by, who make their paths straight.
passages.sermon:
The woman named Folly is loud and knows nothing.
She sits at the door of her house.
Her house stands high in the city.
She sits on a seat in a high place.
She calls out to people who pass by.
She calls to those who walk straight paths.
passages.original: וְֽ֭יָשְׁבָה לְפֶ֣תַח בֵּיתָ֑הּ עַל־ כִּ֝סֵּ֗א מְרֹ֣מֵי קָֽרֶת׃ לִקְרֹ֥א לְעֹֽבְרֵי־ דָ֑רֶךְ הַֽ֝מְיַשְּׁרִ֗ים אֹֽרְחוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.
passages.sermon:
The woman named Folly is loud.
She is naive.
She knows nothing.
She sits at the door of her house.
She sits on a seat in the heights of the city.
She calls out to people who pass by.
She calls to those who make their paths straight.
She says, “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!”
She speaks to the person who lacks judgment.
She invites him inside.
passages.original: מִי־ פֶ֭תִי יָסֻ֣ר הֵ֑נָּה וַחֲסַר־ לֵ֝֗ב וְאָ֣מְרָה לּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is tasty!”
passages.sermon:
A woman sits at the door of her house.
She sits on a seat in the heights of the city.
She calls out to people who pass by.
She calls to those who make their paths straight.
She says, “Stolen water is sweet.”
She says, “Bread eaten in secret is tasty.”
passages.original: מַֽיִם־ גְּנוּבִ֥ים יִמְתָּ֑קוּ וְלֶ֖חֶם סְתָרִ֣ים יִנְעָֽם׃

passages.text: But they do not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
passages.sermon:
The people do not know something important.
The dead are there.
Her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
Sheol is the place of the dead.
Her guests have gone down to that place.
passages.original: וְֽלֹא־ יָ֭דַע כִּֽי־ רְפָאִ֣ים שָׁ֑ם בְּעִמְקֵ֖י שְׁא֣וֹל קְרֻאֶֽיהָ׃פ
